Know who to contact first.

A quick look at hot, warm, and cold leads—and the answers behind each label.

30 seconds · On-screen captions · No audio · Sample leadDownload the video
Read the demo
  1. Hot: contact first. Alex wants to sell as soon as possible and chooses “Selling quickly.” Clear intent and a timeline within three months make this a priority conversation.
  2. Warm: follow up. Change the timing to “Within 3–6 months” and the priority to “Choosing my move date.” Agree on the next step and a follow-up date.
  3. Cold: keep in touch. Change the timing to “Later than 6 months” and the priority to “I’m just exploring.” Ask when another conversation would be welcome.
  4. Confirm the details. The buyer still checks contact and intent, authority to sell, and property details. A priority label does not verify the seller or approve an offer.
